what: New mid-tier Claude with 1M-token context, 128K output, released September 28, 2026.
pitch: A 1M context at $2/$10 per MTok plus $0.20 cache reads makes whole agenda packets and inspection PDFs one call instead of chunk-and-stitch across every Ledger scraper.

name: GPT-6.1 Sol
what: OpenAI's September 29 model priced at $2/$10 per MTok with $0.10 cached input.
pitch: Benchmarked specifically on messy professional PDFs with tables and fine print, at a fifth of Astra's price — the cheapest credible second opinion for permit and assessment PDF parsing.

name: Claude Opus 5.5
what: Long-horizon agentic Claude with 1M context and always-on adaptive thinking, cheaper than Opus 5.
pitch: $4/$20 versus Opus 5's $5/$25, with 128K output and effort-controlled thinking — the model to point Claude Code at for multi-file Ledger Framework refactors that previously stalled.

name: ElevenLabs Speech-to-Text transcript editing (and Eleven v4)
what: Batch and realtime transcription now accept a 2,000-character natural-language edit instruction.
pitch: Fire Watch's weak point is garbled scanner audio: street names, unit numbers, agency jargon. A standing edit instruction normalizes those inside the transcription call, before Haiku classification sees them.
access: paid — ElevenLabs API credits; editing priced per the batch/realtime guides

name: Emergency Mode for News
what: OpenNews/NC Local/Newspack site with disaster checklists, WordPress lite-site plugin, liveblog plugin, microgrants.
pitch: WPR is WordPress plus iframes — a text-only low-bandwidth site plugin and liveblog plugin are the exact missing pieces for a Marathon County tornado or ice-storm outage week.
access: free — open checklists and plugins; $30,000 in microgrants being distributed

name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS (GA)
what: GA text-to-speech models plus voice design, voice replication and a 150+ voice endpoint.
pitch: Flash-Lite TTS is built for high-throughput production, which is what a daily audio edition needs; a designed persistent voice gives WPR one consistent narrator without hiring one.
access: paid — Gemini API TTS models; Flash-Lite TTS positioned for high-volume use

name: OpenAI Decisions API
what: Classification endpoint that answers developer-defined questions from a finite predefined answer set.
pitch: A purpose-built classifier beats prompting a chat model for triage: fixed label sets, text or image input, built for real-time routing — exactly Fire Watch's alert-or-ignore decision.
access: waitlist — limited preview as of September 29, broad release promised shortly

name: Claude Haiku 5.5
what: Anthropic's new small model: faster, far cheaper, and much stronger at classification and summarization.
pitch: WPR runs Haiku on everything high-volume. Input drops from $1.00 to $0.10 per million and output $5.00 to $0.50 on sub-100k prompts, while benchmark scores roughly double.
access: paid — $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for prompts under 100k; $0.50/$2.50 above

name: Cloudflare Clef-omni
what: Open-weight decision model that scores fixed answer options directly from audio, video, image or text.
pitch: Fire Watch transcribes then classifies. Clef-omni answers yes/no questions straight off dispatch audio in under 100ms with no transcript step, and the 30B MoE weights are on Hugging Face for self-hosting.
access: open-source weights plus hosted on Workers AI at $0.15 per million input tokens

name: Deepgram Nova-3 mid-stream keyterm updates
what: Live Nova-3 transcription streams now accept keyterm and formatting changes mid-session without reconnecting.
pitch: Fire Watch and Gavel both need vocabulary that shifts mid-stream: Marathon County street names, agency call signs, board member names. Now swappable live via a Configure message, with Python SDK v7.13.0 support.
access: paid — Deepgram pay-as-you-go; SDK update free; note the 500-token keyterm cap

name: Gemini 4 Argon
what: Google's frontier long-horizon model, now generally available via API for complex coding and multi-step work.
pitch: A solo dev's fallback when Claude Code stalls on a large refactor — Argon is pitched at hundreds-of-files architectural changes. Worth benchmarking before OEC work goes multi-newsroom.
access: paid — introductory $2 per million input, $10 output, 95% off cached input

name: Mistral Voxtral 3 (Transcribe, Realtime, TTS + Voice Agents SDK)
what: New Mistral speech family: diarizing transcription with keyterm biasing, realtime variant, TTS, and a voice-agent SDK.
pitch: Gavel still can't say who spoke. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 does diarization plus context biasing on local names and terms, and the 4B Mini runs $0.0035/min — cheaper than babysitting faster-whisper.
access: paid — public preview API, Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 at $0.0035/min; self-deployment supported

name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe + Granary v2
what: Open-weight 30B-A4B speech model doing promptable transcription, diarization, translation and audio Q&A in one checkpoint.
pitch: Tops open-weight ASR and two diarization leaderboards, labels up to eight speakers across hour-long recordings with word timestamps, and weights plus Granary v2 fine-tuning recipes are free to self-host.
access: open-source — weights and Granary v2 dataset free on Hugging Face; needs GPU

name: Gemini API CLI (gemini-api) beta
what: Stateless, zero-dependency shell client for Gemini models, file analysis and managed agents, built for CI.
pitch: Drops straight into WPR's GitHub Actions cron jobs: no SDK in the repo, media written to disk with only paths printed, --dry-run validation, JSON output and real exit codes.
access: open-source CLI, beta; pay per Gemini API token

name: Claude API version 2026-10-21 and Python SDK 2.0.0
what: New Claude API version with breaking SDK majors across all languages, now Apache 2.0 licensed.
pitch: Every WPR scraper pins the anthropic Python SDK; 2.0.0 defaults to API version 2026-10-21, so pin now or a cron run breaks. Request ceiling also rose to 128MB.
access: free SDK (Apache 2.0); standard API token pricing

name: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra
what: Cheaper, faster OpenAI model specialized for computer use — reading screens and acting across apps.
pitch: Matches GPT-6 Astra on agentic software tasks at a tenth the token price and finishes 3x faster, cheap enough to aim a browser agent at portals that defeat Playwright.
access: paid — API as gpt-6.1-terra, 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra pricing
